explanations: The soprano has the highest vocal range of all the classical voice types and takes the top line in four-part harmony.
The tenor is the highest male chest voice, lying between the countertenor and the baritone in range.
The baritone lies between the bass and the tenor and is the most common male voice; its name is Greek for low sounding.
Soprano, tenor and baritone are three of the singing voice types into which a singer is placed by voice classification.

sources.excerpt: A soprano (Italian pronunciation: [soˈpraːno]) is a type of classical singing voice and has the highest vocal range of all voice types.
In four-part chorale style harmony, the soprano takes the highest part, which often encompasses the melody.
The tenor is a type of male singing voice whose vocal range lies between the countertenor and baritone voice types. It is the highest male chest-voice type.

Composers typically write music for the tenor in the range from the second B below middle C, to the G above middle C (i.e. B2 to G4) in choral music – and from the second B-flat below middle C, to the C above middle C (B♭2 to C5) in operatic music – but the range can extend at either end.
A baritone is a type of classical male singing voice whose vocal range lies between the bass and the tenor voice types.
It is the most common human male voice.
The term originates from the Greek βαρύτονος (barýtonos), meaning "low sounding".
A voice type is a classification of the human singing voice into perceivable categories or groups.
